0&-\frac{\epsilon}{s}&0\\
\frac{2(2\epsilon-1)}{st(s+t)}&\frac{2(1-2\epsilon)}{s^{2}(s+t)}&-\frac{s+t+\epsilon t}{s(s+t)}\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad A_{t}=\begin{pmatrix}-\frac{\epsilon}{t}&0&0\\
0&0&0\\
\frac{2(1-2\epsilon)}{t^{2}(s+t)}&\frac{2(2\epsilon-1)}{st(s+t)}&-\frac{s+t+\epsilon s}{t(s+t)}\\
\end{pmatrix}\,.

(1170)

We verify the integrability conditions,

\displaystyle A_{s}\cdot A_{t}-A_{t}\cdot A_{s}+\partial_{t}A_{s}-\partial_{s}A_{t}=0\,,

(1171)

and the scaling relation,

\displaystyle s\,A_{s}+t\,A_{t}=\text{diag}(-\epsilon,-\epsilon,-2-\epsilon)\,.

(1172)

The diagonal entries on the RHS of the scaling relation match the power counting of the integrals in
\vec{g}
in units of
s
.

c) We express
\vec{f}
in terms of
\vec{g}
as
\vec{f}=T^{-1}\cdot\vec{g}
by IBP-reducing the integrals in eq. (
785
).
39
39

39

We use the inverse of
T
to match the convention of section
30.3
for the gauge transformation.
We obtain

\displaystyle T^{-1}=c(\epsilon)\,\begin{pmatrix}0&0&st\\
0&\frac{2\epsilon-1}{\epsilon}&0\\
\frac{2\epsilon-1}{\epsilon}&0&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,.

(1173)

The new basis
\vec{f}
satisfies a system of DEs in canonical form,

\displaystyle\begin{cases}\partial_{s}\vec{f}(s,t;\epsilon)=\epsilon\,B_{s}(s,t)\cdot\vec{f}(s,t;\epsilon)\,,\\
\partial_{t}\vec{f}(s,t;\epsilon)=\epsilon\,B_{t}(s,t)\cdot\vec{f}(s,t;\epsilon)\,,\\
\end{cases}

(1174)

where

\displaystyle B_{s}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{s+t}-\frac{1}{s}&\frac{2}{s+t}-\frac{2}{s}&\frac{2}{s+t}\\
0&-\frac{1}{s}&0\\
0&0&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad B_{t}=\begin{pmatrix}\frac{1}{s+t}-\frac{1}{t}&\frac{2}{s+t}&\frac{2}{s+t}-\frac{2}{t}\\
0&0&0\\
0&0&-\frac{1}{t}\\
\end{pmatrix}\,.

(1175)

We compute
B_{s}
and
B_{t}
as in point b, or through the gauge transformation

\displaystyle\epsilon\,B_{s}=T^{-1}\cdot A_{s}\cdot T-T^{-1}\cdot\partial_{s}T\,,

(1176)

and similarly for
t
. From eq. (
1175
) we see that the symbol alphabet of this family is
\{s,t,s+t\}
.
Thanks to the factorisation of
\epsilon
on the RHS of the canonical DEs (
1174
), the integrability conditions split into

\displaystyle B_{s}\cdot B_{t}-B_{t}\cdot B_{s}=0\,,\qquad\qquad\partial_{s}B_{t}-\partial_{t}B_{s}=0\,.

(1177)

The scaling relation is given by

\displaystyle s\,B_{s}+t\,B_{t}=-\mathds{1}_{3}\,.

(1178)

d) Viewed as a function of
s
and
x=t/s
,
\vec{f}
satisfies the canonical DEs

\displaystyle\begin{cases}\partial_{s}\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)=\epsilon\,C_{s}(s,x)\cdot\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)\,,\\
\partial_{x}\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)=\epsilon\,C_{x}(s,x)\cdot\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)\,,\\
\end{cases}

(1179)

where
C_{s}
and
C_{x}
are related to
B_{s}
and
B_{t}
in (
1175
) through the chain rule,

\displaystyle C_{x}=s\,B_{t}\Bigl|_{t=xs}\,,\qquad\qquad C_{s}=B_{s}+\frac{t}{s}\,B_{t}\Bigl|_{t=xs}\,.

(1180)

We observe that
C_{x}
is a function of
x
only, and
C_{s}
of
s
. Thanks to this separation of variables, we can straightforwardly rewrite the canonical DEs in differential form,

\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\,\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)=\epsilon\,\bigl[\mathrm{d}\,\tilde{C}(s,x)\bigr]\cdot\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)\,.

(1181)

The connection matrix
\tilde{C}
is given by a linear combination of logarithms of the alphabet letters
\alpha_{1}=s
,
\alpha_{2}=x
and
\alpha_{3}=1+x
,

\displaystyle\tilde{C}(s,x)=\sum_{k=1}^{3}C_{k}\,\log\alpha_{k}(s,x)\,,

(1182)

with constant matrix coefficients,

\displaystyle C_{1}=-\mathds{1}_{3}\,,\qquad C_{2}=\begin{pmatrix}-1&0&-2\\
0&0&0\\
0&0&-1\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\qquad C_{3}=\begin{pmatrix}1&2&2\\
0&0&0\\
0&0&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,.

(1183)

e) We expand the pure integrals
\vec{f}
as a Taylor series around
\epsilon=0
,
40
40

40

The factor
c(\epsilon)
in the definition of the pure integrals (
785
) is chosen such that they are finite at
\epsilon=0
.

\displaystyle\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)=\sum_{w\geq 0}\epsilon^{w}\,\vec{f}^{(w)}(s,x)\,,

(1184)

and define the weight-
w
boundary values at
s=-1
and
x=1
as
\vec{b}^{(w)}=\vec{f}^{(w)}(-1,1)
.
Using eq. (
621
) for the bubble-type integrals we obtain

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &f_{2}(s,x;\epsilon)=-1+\epsilon\,\log(-s)-\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{12}\left(6\log^{2}(-s)-\pi^{2}\right)\\
&\phantom{f_{2}(s,x;\epsilon)=\,}+\frac{\epsilon^{3}}{12}\left(2\,\log^{3}(-s)-\pi^{2}\log(-s)+28\,\zeta_{3}\right)+\mathcal{O}\bigl(\epsilon^{4}\bigr)\,.\\
\end{aligned}

(1185)

The expression for
f_{3}(s,x;\epsilon)
is obtained by trading
s
for
t=sx
in
f_{2}(s,x;\epsilon)
.
We leave
b_{1}^{(w)}
as free parameters. The weight-
0
boundary values are thus given by
\vec{b}^{(0)}=(b_{1}^{(0)},-1,-1)^{\top}
. We can now solve the canonical DEs in terms of symbols. In order to do so, we note that the canonical DEs (
1181
) imply the following DEs for the coefficients of the
\epsilon
expansion,

\displaystyle\mathrm{d}\,f_{i}^{(w)}(s,x)=\sum_{k=1}^{3}\left[\sum_{j=1}^{3}(C_{k})_{ij}\,f_{j}^{(w-1)}(s,x)\right]\,\mathrm{d}\log\alpha_{k}(s,x)\,.

(1186)

The iteration starts from
\vec{f}^{(0)}=\vec{b}^{(0)}
. We spelled out all indices in eq. (
1186
) to facilitate the comparison against the recursive definition of the symbol given by eqs. (
702
) and (
703
). From this, we find the following recursive formula for the symbol of the solution to the canonical DEs:

\displaystyle\mathcal{S}\Bigl(f_{i}^{(w)}\Bigr)=\sum_{k=1}^{3}\sum_{j=1}^{3}(C_{k})_{ij}\,\biggl[\mathcal{S}\Bigl(f_{j}^{(w-1)}\Bigr),\,\alpha_{k}\biggr]\,,

(1187)

starting at weight
w=0
with
\mathcal{S}\bigl(f_{i}^{(0)}\bigr)=b^{(0)}_{i}[]
(we recall that
[]
denotes the empty symbol).
With a slight abuse of notation, we may rewrite this in a more compact form as

\displaystyle\mathcal{S}\bigl(\vec{f}^{(w)}\bigr)=\sum_{k=1}^{3}C_{k}\cdot\left[\mathcal{S}\bigl(\vec{f}^{(w-1)}\bigr),\,\alpha_{k}\right]\,.

(1188)

At transcendental weight 1 we thus have that

\displaystyle\mathcal{S}\bigl(\vec{f}^{(1)}\bigr)=C_{1}\cdot\vec{b}^{(0)}\,[s]+C_{2}\cdot\vec{b}^{(0)}\,[x]+C_{3}\cdot\vec{b}^{(0)}\,[1+x]\,.

(1189)

Since
[1+x]
is the symbol of
\log(1+x)
,
\vec{f}^{(1)}(x)
would diverge at

unless the coefficients of
[1+x]
vanish. The finiteness at
x=-1
thus implies

\displaystyle C_{3}\cdot\vec{b}^{(0)}=0\,,

(1190)

which fixes
b_{1}^{(0)}=4
. We now have everything we need to write down the symbol of the solution up to any order in
\epsilon
. For
f_{1}
, for instance, we obtain

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\mathcal{S}\left(f_{1}\right)=4\,[]-2\,\epsilon\bigl(2\,[s]+[x]\bigr)+2\,\epsilon^{2}\bigl(2\,[s,s]+[s,x]+[x,s]\bigr)\\
&\,-2\epsilon^{3}\Bigl(2\,[s,s,s]+[s,s,x]+[s,x,s]+[x,s,s]-[x,x,x]+[x,x,1+x]\Bigr)+\mathcal{O}\bigl(\epsilon^{4}\bigr)\,.\end{aligned}

(1191)

f) The dependence on
s
is given by an overall factor of
(-s)^{-\epsilon}
,
41
41

41

The minus sign in front of

ensures the positivity in the Euclidean region, where

.
which is fixed by dimensional analysis. We thus define

\displaystyle\vec{f}(s,x;\epsilon)=(-s)^{-\epsilon}\,\vec{h}(x;\epsilon)\,,

(1192)

where
\vec{h}(x;\epsilon)
does not depend on

around

as in (

\displaystyle\partial_{x}\,\vec{h}^{(w)}(x)=\left[\frac{C_{2}}{x}+\frac{C_{3}}{1+x}\right]\cdot\vec{h}^{(w-1)}(x)\,.

(1193)

Equation (
1185
) implies that

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &h_{2}(x;\epsilon)=-1+\epsilon^{2}\frac{\pi^{2}}{12}+\epsilon^{3}\frac{7}{3}\zeta_{3}+\mathcal{O}\bigl(\epsilon^{4}\bigr)\,,\\
&h_{3}(x;\epsilon)=-1+\epsilon\,\log(x)+\frac{\epsilon^{2}}{12}\left[\pi^{2}-6\,\log^{2}(x)\right]\\
&\phantom{h_{3}(x;\epsilon)=\,}+\frac{\epsilon^{3}}{12}\left[2\,\log^{3}(x)-\pi^{2}\log(x)+28\,\zeta_{3}\right]+\mathcal{O}\bigl(\epsilon^{4}\bigr)\,,\end{aligned}

(1194)

which give us the boundary values
\vec{e}^{(w)}=\vec{h}^{(w)}(1)
for the second and third integral. We have determined above that
e_{1}^{(0)}=4
, and we leave the remaining
e_{1}^{(w)}
’s as free parameters.
Integrating both sides of eq. (
1193
) gives

\displaystyle\vec{h}^{(w)}(x)=\int_{1}^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d}x^{\prime}}{x^{\prime}}\,C_{2}\cdot\vec{h}^{(w-1)}(x^{\prime})+\int_{1}^{x}\frac{\mathrm{d}x^{\prime}}{1+x^{\prime}}\,C_{3}\cdot\vec{h}^{(w-1)}(x^{\prime})+\vec{e}^{(w)}\,,

(1195)

starting from
\vec{h}^{(0)}=\vec{e}^{(0)}
.
For arbitrary values of the undetermined

’s, the second integral on the RHS of eq. (

) diverges at

. We can thus fix the remaining boundary values by requiring that

\displaystyle\lim_{x\to-1}C_{3}\cdot\vec{h}^{(w)}(x)=0\,,

(1196)

order by order in
\epsilon
.
For instance, at weight one we have that

\displaystyle C_{3}\cdot\vec{h}^{(1)}(x)=\left(e_{1}^{(1)},\,0,\,0\right)^{\top}\,.

(1197)

The finiteness at
x=-1
thus fixes
e_{1}^{(1)}=0
. Iterating this up to weight 3 yields

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &h_{1}(x;\epsilon)=4+\epsilon\bigl[-2\,\log(x)\bigr]+\epsilon^{2}\biggl[-\frac{4\pi^{2}}{3}\biggr]+\epsilon^{3}\biggl[2\,\text{Li}_{3}(-x)-2\,\log(x)\,\text{Li}_{2}(-x)\\
&\ +\frac{1}{3}\log^{3}(x)-\log(x)^{2}\log(1+x)+\frac{7\pi^{2}}{6}\log(x)-\pi^{2}\log(1+x)-\frac{34}{3}\zeta_{3}\biggr]+\mathcal{O}\bigl(\epsilon^{4}\bigr)\,.\end{aligned}

(1198)

g) Equation (
660
) is related to eq. (

) through
h_{1}=\epsilon^{2}st\mathrm{e}^{\epsilon\gamma_{\text{E}}}(-s)^{\epsilon}F_{4}

\displaystyle\begin{aligned} &\mathrm{Li}_{2}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)=-\mathrm{Li}_{2}(-x)-\frac{1}{2}\log^{2}(x)-\zeta_{2}\,,\\
&\mathrm{Li}_{3}\left(-\frac{1}{x}\right)=\mathrm{Li}_{3}(-x)+\frac{1}{3!}\log^{3}(x)+\zeta_{2}\log(x)\,,\end{aligned}

(1199)

for

.

Chapter 6
Conventions and useful formulae

•

Index and metric conventions:

\displaystyle\eta_{\mu\nu}

\displaystyle=\text{diag}(+,-,-,-)\,,\qquad p_{\mu}p^{\mu}=p_{0}^{2}-{\vec{p}}^{2}\,,

\displaystyle\epsilon_{12}

\displaystyle=\epsilon_{\dot{1}\dot{2}}=\epsilon^{21}=\epsilon^{\dot{2}\dot{1}}=+1\,,\quad\epsilon_{21}=\epsilon_{\dot{2}\dot{1}}=\epsilon^{12}=\epsilon^{\dot{1}\dot{2}}=-1\,,

\displaystyle(\bar{\sigma}^{\mu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}

\displaystyle=(\mathds{1},-\vec{\sigma})\,,\quad(\sigma^{\mu})_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}=\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\,\epsilon_{{\dot{\alpha}}{\dot{\beta}}}\,(\bar{\sigma}^{\mu})^{{\dot{\beta}}\beta}=(\mathds{1},\vec{\sigma})\,,

\displaystyle(\bar{\sigma}_{\mu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}

\displaystyle=(\mathds{1},\vec{\sigma})\,,\quad(\sigma_{\mu})_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}=(\mathds{1},-\vec{\sigma})\,,

\displaystyle\sigma_{1}

\displaystyle=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\
1&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\quad\sigma_{2}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\mathrm{i}\\
\mathrm{i}&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\quad\sigma_{3}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\
0&-1\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,

\displaystyle\chi^{\alpha}

\displaystyle=\epsilon^{\alpha\beta}\,\chi_{\beta}\,,\qquad\tilde{\chi}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}=\epsilon^{{\dot{\alpha}}{\dot{\beta}}}\,\tilde{\chi}_{\beta}\,,

\displaystyle(\chi_{\alpha})^{\ast}

\displaystyle=\tilde{\chi}_{{\dot{\alpha}}}\,,\qquad(\chi^{\alpha}\,\psi^{\beta})^{\dagger}=(\psi^{\beta})^{\dagger}\,(\chi^{\alpha})^{\dagger}\,.

•

(Anti)-symmetrisation:

\displaystyle A_{(\mu}\,B_{\nu)}\coloneqq\frac{1}{2}\,(A_{\mu}B_{\nu}+A_{\nu}B_{\mu})\,,\qquad A_{[\mu}\,B_{\nu]}\coloneqq\frac{1}{2}\,(A_{\mu}B_{\nu}-A_{\nu}B_{\mu})\,.

•

Spinor helicity relations:

\displaystyle p^{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}

\displaystyle=\lambda^{\alpha}\,\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}\,,\qquad p_{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}=\epsilon_{{\dot{\alpha}}{\dot{\beta}}}\,\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\,\lambda^{\beta}\,\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\beta}}}\,,\quad\lambda_{\alpha}=\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}\,\lambda^{\beta}\,,\quad\tilde{\lambda}_{{\dot{\alpha}}}=\epsilon_{{\dot{\alpha}}{\dot{\beta}}}\,\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\beta}}}\,,

\displaystyle u_{+}(p)

\displaystyle=v_{-}(p)=\begin{pmatrix}\lambda_{\alpha}\\
0\\
\end{pmatrix}\eqqcolon|p\rangle\,,\quad u_{-}(p)=v_{+}(p)=\begin{pmatrix}0\\
\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}\\
\end{pmatrix}\eqqcolon|p]\,,

\displaystyle\bar{u}_{+}(p)

\displaystyle=\bar{v}_{-}(p)=(0\,\,\,\tilde{\lambda}_{{\dot{\alpha}}})\eqqcolon[p|\,,\quad\bar{u}_{-}(p)=\bar{v}_{+}(p)=(\lambda^{\alpha}\,\,\,0)\eqqcolon\langle p|\,,

\displaystyle\langle\lambda_{i}\,\lambda_{j}\rangle

\displaystyle\coloneqq\lambda_{i}^{\alpha}\,\lambda_{j\,\alpha}\,,\qquad[\tilde{\lambda}_{i}\,\tilde{\lambda}_{j}]\coloneqq\tilde{\lambda}_{i\,{\dot{\alpha}}}\,\tilde{\lambda}_{j}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}\,.

Using the chiral representation of the Dirac matrices, we have

\displaystyle\not{p}

\displaystyle=p_{\mu}\,\gamma^{\mu}=\begin{pmatrix}0&p_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\\
p^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}&0\\
\end{pmatrix}\,,\quad\quad p_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\coloneqq p_{\mu}\,(\sigma^{\mu})_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\,,

\displaystyle p^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}

\displaystyle=\epsilon^{\alpha\beta}\,\epsilon^{{\dot{\alpha}}{\dot{\beta}}}\,p_{\beta{\dot{\beta}}}=p_{\mu}\,(\bar{\sigma}^{\mu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}\,.

We furthermore note

\displaystyle[i|\gamma^{\mu}|j\rangle

\displaystyle=\langle j|\gamma^{\mu}|i]\,,\quad\langle p|\gamma^{\mu}|p]=\lambda^{\alpha}\,\sigma^{\mu}_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\,\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}=2\,p^{\mu}\,,

\displaystyle[i|\gamma^{\mu}|j\rangle\,\langle l|\gamma_{\mu}|k]

\displaystyle=2\,[ik]\,\langle lj\rangle\,.

•

The generators of the Lorentz group in the spinor representation are given by

\displaystyle(\sigma^{\mu\nu})_{\alpha}{}^{\beta}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\,\Bigl((\sigma^{\mu})_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\,({\bar{\sigma}}^{\nu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\beta}-(\sigma^{\nu})_{\alpha{\dot{\alpha}}}\,({\bar{\sigma}}^{\mu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\beta}\Bigr)\,,

\displaystyle({\bar{\sigma}}^{\mu\nu})^{\alpha}{}_{\dot{\beta}}

\displaystyle=\frac{1}{4}\,\Bigl(({\bar{\sigma}}^{\mu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}\,({\sigma}^{\nu})_{\alpha{\dot{\beta}}}-({\bar{\sigma}}^{\nu})^{{\dot{\alpha}}\alpha}\,({\sigma}^{\mu})^{\alpha{\dot{\beta}}}\Bigr)\,.

•

Complex conjugation properties:

\displaystyle(\lambda^{\alpha})^{\ast}=\tilde{\lambda}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}\,,\qquad\langle ij\rangle^{\ast}=(\lambda_{i}^{\alpha}\,\lambda_{j\,\alpha})^{\ast}=(\tilde{\lambda}_{i}^{{\dot{\alpha}}}\,\tilde{\lambda}_{j\,{\dot{\alpha}}})^{\ast}=-[ij]\,.

•

Useful trace identities:

\displaystyle\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[\not{a}\,\not{b}\,\not{c}\,\not{d}]

\displaystyle=4\,[\,(a\cdot b)(c\cdot d)-(a\cdot c)(b\cdot d)+(a\cdot d)(b\cdot c)\,]\,,

\displaystyle\mathop{\mathrm{Tr}}[\not{a}\,\not{b}\,]

\displaystyle=4\,(a\cdot b)\,.

•
